q: What is one basis point?
explain: A basis point is one hundredth of one per cent, so 20bp is 0.20%.

q: A pension scheme's promise to pay members in future is, for the scheme, a…
explain: A liability is something owed. The scheme invests assets to meet it.

q: In a segregated mandate, who owns the securities?
explain: The client owns the assets directly; the manager only has authority to manage them under an agreement.

q: What does the investment management agreement (IMA) do?
options: Sets the legal terms, guidelines and fees for a mandate
explain: It is the contract: objectives, restrictions, reporting, fees and termination.

q: A pooled fund differs from a segregated mandate because…
options: Many investors share one portfolio and the same terms
explain: A pooled fund mixes investors' money in one vehicle with standard terms.

q: A defined benefit (DB) scheme promises…
options: A pot whose size depends on markets
A pension set by a formula, whatever markets do
A fixed lump sum from the state
explain: In DB the employer-backed scheme bears the investment risk; in defined contribution the member does.

q: Liability-driven investment (LDI) mainly aims to…
options: Make scheme assets move in line with the value of its liabilities
explain: LDI hedges the interest-rate and inflation sensitivity of the liabilities.

q: Why does an investor hold a money market fund?
options: To park cash safely with daily access
explain: It is for capital preservation and liquidity, with a modest yield.

q: Tracking error measures…
options: Days needed to sell the portfolio
How far returns vary from the benchmark
explain: It is the volatility of the difference between portfolio and benchmark returns.

q: An investment consultant is paid by…
options: The asset manager, per mandate won
explain: Consultants advise the asset owner; that is what makes their manager ratings credible.

q: Which fee is charged only if performance exceeds a stated level?
explain: Incentive fees are a share of return or of excess return over a benchmark or target.

q: OCIO stands for…
explain: The client delegates running all or part of its portfolio to a provider.

q: In Goldman's filings, AUS means…
explain: AUS includes discretionary assets and advisory relationships where a fee is earned.

q: A DDQ is…
explain: A standard set of questions a client or consultant sends to assess a manager.

q: LGPS is…
explain: The UK's funded public-sector scheme for local government workers, organised into pools.

q: LVNAV describes…
options: A type of money market fund
explain: Low-volatility net asset value: a short-term money market fund structure.

q: In UK wealth management, MPS means…
explain: Ready-made portfolios run on platforms for advisers' clients.

q: The matching adjustment is relevant mainly to…
explain: It lets insurers recognise part of the yield on assets that match long-term liabilities.

q: A 'breakpoint' in a fee schedule is…
options: An asset level above which a lower rate applies
explain: Tiered fees charge lower marginal rates on larger slices.

q: Goldman describes the Client Solutions Group as serving which two client types?
explain: It develops client relationships and delivers investment solutions for institutional and third-party wealth clients.

q: What does the 2027 London CSG listing say about day-to-day duties?
explain: It contains no team-specific duties, deadline or salary.

q: How long is the Summer Analyst programme?
explain: Goldman states nine to ten weeks.

q: How many business/location combinations may an applicant apply to in a year?
explain: Up to four; extra applications are automatically withdrawn.

q: Which is on Goldman's published task list for a junior London CSG sales-support hire?
options: Preparing and following up client and prospect meetings
explain: Meeting preparation and follow-up, client queries and working with product specialists are listed; investment decisions are not.

q: Who decides which bonds go into a client's portfolio?
options: The portfolio manager, within the client's guidelines
explain: Coverage staff explain and coordinate; investment decisions belong to portfolio managers.

q: Which role works with investment consultants to build a pipeline for sales teams?
explain: Goldman describes Consultant Relations this way.

q: How does client coverage in asset management differ from markets sales and trading?
options: It sells an ongoing investment service, not individual trades
explain: Asset management clients hire the firm to manage money over time and pay an ongoing fee.

q: What does Goldman's Client Coverage Group definition emphasise?
options: Retaining, expanding and supporting existing client relationships
explain: That is the wording of the published definition.

q: A London Benelux 'Client Solutions Group' advertisement says the team is responsible for…
options: Both new business development and existing institutional relationships
explain: So the CSG name does not exclude relationship management.

q: From which office does Goldman advertise German institutional sales roles?
explain: The 2027 Frankfurt CSG Institutional Sales listing is for a German speaker.

q: Which language does the London-based Benelux CSG role require?
explain: Native Dutch essential, French an advantage.

q: Why does a single hierarchy misdescribe the client business?
options: Geography, client segment, product line and function overlap
explain: A matrix is closer to the evidence than a tree.

q: Where did Goldman move its Iberia distribution head and her London team in June 2021?
explain: Madrid.

q: What did Goldman do with its Nordic sales teams in May 2020?
options: Merged institutional sales and third-party distribution into one organisation
explain: One Nordic organisation selling all asset classes to all client types.

q: Liquidity Solutions is best described as…
options: A client business organised around a product line
explain: It has global leadership and serves several client types with cash products.

q: Which acquisition made the Netherlands a major Goldman Sachs Asset Management location?
explain: More than 900 NN IP staff joined in April 2022.

q: What is publicly established about who currently leads the Middle East client business?
options: It is run from New York
Nothing: the previous head left in September 2025 and no successor is established
explain: The departure is public; the current head is not.

q: Is Goldman's OCIO business UK-only?
explain: $480bn of OCIO assets globally at 31 March 2026, with large US mandates.

q: Roughly how large was the BAE Systems pension schemes mandate announced in September 2023?
explain: About £23bn of UK defined benefit assets.

q: Who advised the BAE Systems trustees in the tender?
explain: Redington advised the trustees; PwC advised the sponsor.

q: Who oversaw the Shell pension entities' tender?
explain: Isio oversaw it, with each fund making its own decision.

q: Within Goldman, the OCIO teams sit in…
explain: They work with sales and relationship professionals but are part of an investing group.

q: Before a fiduciary manager runs 20% or more of a UK trust-based scheme's assets, trustees must…
options: Run a competitive tender with at least three unconnected providers
explain: The duty sits in pensions regulations overseen by TPR since October 2022.

q: Is transferring the client's in-house team to Goldman a universal feature of its OCIO mandates?
options: No: it is reported in some of the largest deals only
explain: Reported for BAE and UPS; not for Short Brothers or Calor.

q: Which statement about Goldman and 2026 fiduciary awards is accurate?
options: It won at the European Pensions Awards and the Irish Pensions Awards, but not Fiduciary Manager of the Year at the UK Pensions Awards
Awards are not given in this field
explain: Two wins and one category that went to Van Lanschot Kempen.

q: What does a public UK scheme report show about a typical fiduciary fee structure?
options: An asset-based fiduciary fee, with underlying manager fees negotiated by the fiduciary manager and LDI invoiced separately
explain: That structure is documented in a published scheme report.

q: Goldman's 2025 filing shows advisory and OCIO alternative accounts earning about…
explain: 17bp against 77bp on funds and discretionary accounts.

q: Who are the direct clients of a Third Party Wealth team?
options: Private banks, wealth managers, advisers and multi-managers
explain: The team sells to professional intermediaries who invest for their own clients.

q: A fund is added to a wealth manager's approved list. What follows?
options: Permission for advisers to buy; assets depend on their choices
explain: Listing is necessary, not sufficient.

q: What do Goldman's filings call the channel that Third Party Wealth serves?
explain: Third-party distributed long-term AUS was $714bn at 30 September 2026.

q: How many active ETFs did Goldman say it launched in Europe in 2025?
explain: Stated in its April 2026 announcement.

q: What happened to the head of EMEA Third Party Wealth in April 2026?
options: Reported to be leaving for a competitor, with no successor publicly named by the cutoff
explain: So no EMEA head should be named.

q: Under the UK Consumer Duty, which outcome bears most directly on fund pricing?
explain: Price and value is one of the four outcomes.

q: What is the G-Series?
options: A suite of open-ended (evergreen) private-markets funds
A range of money market funds
explain: Sold through private wealth and select third-party distributors.

q: What matters most to a corporate treasurer holding operating cash?
explain: Cash may be needed tomorrow; yield comes third.

q: In Q3 2026, Goldman's liquidity products had…
explain: Long-term assets took in $97bn in the same quarter.

q: About what share of sterling money market fund assets is in EU-domiciled funds?
explain: They are sold in the UK under temporary permissions.

q: Goldman's 2025 average effective fee on liquidity products was…
explain: The lowest of the four asset classes.

q: Is a French-language requirement for Liquidity Solutions roles publicly supported?
explain: The one French-speaker advert found belonged to a French third-party wealth sales team.

q: Why is an insurer a different client from a pension scheme?
options: Regulatory capital and accounting shape what it can hold
explain: Capital charges and matching rules make asset choice a balance-sheet decision.

q: How much in insurers' general-account assets does Goldman say it manages?
explain: As of 31 December 2025.

q: In Goldman's 2026 insurance survey, what share of respondents planned to increase private-asset allocations?
explain: 434 chief investment and finance officers were polled.

q: When do the amended EU Solvency II rules take effect?
explain: Directive (EU) 2025/2.

q: £500m managed at 20bp for a full year gives a gross management fee of…
£200m at 35bp for a year gives…
A £500m mandate at 20bp is half funded in month 1 and fully funded from month 7. Year-one fee?
explain: Six months on £250m (£250k) plus six months on £500m (£500k).

q: Tiered fee: 25bp to £250m, 20bp to £500m, 15bp above. Annual fee on £600m?
Tiered fee: 25bp to £250m, 20bp to £500m, 15bp above. Annual fee on £400m?
£1bn at 15bp; the client withdraws £400m at the start of month 7. Fee for the year?
explain: Six months on £1bn (£750k) plus six on £600m (£450k).

q: £800m at 12bp for six months gives…
explain: Half of £960,000.

q: A private fund charges 100bp on committed capital. On a £50m commitment with only 10% drawn, the annual fee is…
explain: The fee base is the commitment, not the amount drawn.

q: What share of Goldman's 2025 net revenues came from the Asset & Wealth Management segment?
What share of Goldman's 2025 net revenues came from the asset management business alone (excluding wealth management)?
Total AUS at 30 September 2026 was…
explain: $3,046bn long-term plus $1,051bn liquidity.

q: Which asset class had Goldman's highest average effective management fee in 2025?
explain: Alternatives 58bp, equity 54bp, fixed income 17bp, liquidity 14bp.

q: Why is a 'commitment' to a private fund not the same as fee-paying assets?
options: Fees may start only when capital is drawn and invested, depending on the fund's fee base
explain: $105bn of commitments raised 2020–2025 was not yet fee-earning.

q: Retaining a client that was about to leave…
options: Avoids a loss; it does not add revenue
explain: Retained revenue is not incremental revenue.

q: What does Goldman disclose about Client Solutions Group revenue?
explain: No revenue, assets, flows, headcount or fee rates are published for the group or any EMEA client team.

q: Which channel had the largest long-term net inflows in the first nine months of 2026?
explain: Partly helped by acquired ETF assets.

q: 'Sales wins, relationship management retains' is…
options: A first approximation; real teams overlap
explain: Published Goldman advertisements show one team doing both.

q: Which task is in Goldman's official description of client coverage work?
options: Coordinating account openings, restructures and terminations
explain: Along with queries, reporting, questionnaires and audit requests.

q: A client asks a junior a technical question the junior cannot answer. Best response?
options: Say you do not know, find out from the specialist and reply by a stated time
explain: Competence includes knowing where your knowledge ends.

q: Is the £52k versus £48k analyst pay gap established by a public source?
options: No, it is one person's account
explain: No credible public source gives London analyst pay for this business.

q: Why can a won mandate still disappoint commercially?
options: Funding can be delayed, partial or reversed, and fees follow assets actually managed
explain: Awarded is not funded.

q: Which is an observable behaviour of reliability?
options: Doing what you said, by when you said
explain: Trust has to be visible in behaviour.

q: After appointing Goldman as OCIO, the BAE Systems trustee…
explain: The scheme's 2026 statement records Gallagher advising the trustee.

q: Which real case shows a fiduciary client ending a mandate with Goldman?
explain: A €7bn mandate appointed in 2006.

q: When is a client right to leave a manager?
options: When its needs have changed or the manager no longer meets them, even if the relationship is warm
explain: Retention is not automatically a good outcome.

q: Why does a good relationship not remove due diligence?
options: Trustees and selectors have duties that require evidence
explain: Soft information tells you which question to ask; hard information has to answer it.

q: What happens if relationship knowledge stays in one person's head?
options: The institution loses it when that person moves
explain: Notes and handovers turn personal knowledge into the firm's knowledge.

q: What did the Bank of England do on 5 November 2026?
explain: The first increase since August 2023, by 8 votes to 1.

q: UK defined benefit schemes' aggregate funding ratio on the PPF measure at end October 2026 was about…
explain: 133.7%, a £275.4bn surplus.

q: The Pension Schemes Act 2026 requires DC default arrangements to reach…
options: £25bn by 2030, or be on track by 2035
explain: Royal Assent 29 April 2026.

q: How many LGPS pools are there after the 2026 reform?
explain: Down from eight.

q: What did the Bank of England's July 2026 report say about private credit?
options: It remains vulnerable to tighter financing, with elevated redemption requests in some retail funds
explain: Some funds limited withdrawals.

q: A market change has happened. What should a coverage professional do first?
options: Work out how it changes this client's position and decisions
explain: Not every market change is a reason to sell something.

q: In 2025, UK buy-ins were notable for…
options: A record number of deals but lower total premium
explain: 370 deals, about £38bn.

q: Which competitor reports over $400bn of OCIO and fiduciary assets and won an £8bn UK mandate in July 2026?
explain: British Coal Staff Superannuation Scheme.

q: Who completed the acquisition of Schroders in October 2026?
explain: A £9.9bn deal.

q: What is State Street's asset manager called since June 2025?
explain: Renamed on 30 June 2025.

q: 'Global platform' is a weak differentiator because…
options: Several competitors can say the same; you need a specific capability and why the client cares
explain: Test each claim: evidence, do competitors offer it, why it matters, where Goldman is less suitable.

q: Goldman's External Investing Group is relevant to OCIO because…
options: It selects external managers, with over $528bn across strategies
explain: It supports the open-architecture claim.

q: Who is publicly described as head of the Client Solutions Group?
explain: Nachmann heads Asset & Wealth Management.

q: In EMEA, 'Executive Director' at Goldman corresponds to which corporate title?
explain: Listings titled Executive Director carry the Vice President corporate title.

q: What is Goldman's stated first-round step for campus applicants?
options: A phone call with a partner
A video interview of about 30 minutes
explain: The site calls it the HireVue interview.

q: Which evidence status fits 'OCIO exists only in the UK'?
explain: Goldman's own disclosures show a global business.

q: Which evidence status fits 'what you say in the video interview decides your team'?
explain: It comes from one person and is not published.

q: Which evidence status fits 'BAE Systems is an OCIO client'?
explain: Goldman announced it by press release.

q: Which evidence status fits 'asset management is about 30% of Goldman's revenue'?
explain: True of the AWM segment (28.6%), not of asset management alone (11.6%).

q: Which evidence status fits 'assessment centres are now in person and ask more about AI'?
explain: No official source confirms it for this programme.
